basis: Immune dysregulation; alveolar hemorrhage/respiratory failure and marrow hypocellularity each in 1/1 patient; limited evidence. Diabetes and hypothyroidism are separate diseases.
Benign epidermal neoplasm arising on the eyelid; both eyelid and skin axes apply.
Predominantly gonadal germ cell malignancy, outside the axes; CNS and other extragonadal sites are site-specific subtypes, not shared organ involvement.
Defined by mitral valve disease, skeletal fusions and hearing loss. Reflux in 5/6 is a separately diagnosed disorder; feeding difficulty alone does not establish GI damage.
Malignant notochordal tumor arising in the axial skeleton; neural compression is not universal defining involvement.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; lissencephaly 9/9 and retinal dysplasia 6/6. Gonadal dysgenesis alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Site-unspecified malignant teratoma, predominantly gonadal and outside the axes; CNS, gastric and mediastinal origins belong to particular subtypes.
CFTR-related injury of bile ducts and liver defines this concept; pulmonary and pancreatic CF manifestations belong to the underlying disease.
Hearing impairment, elliptocytosis and nephrocalcinosis define the syndrome; cleft hard palate reported in 2/2 supports GI involvement. Neurodevelopmental frequency is uncertain.
Complement receptor dysfunction defines an immunodeficiency; no common direct damage to another organ is established.
Congenital fistula directly connects the malformed rectum and prostatic urethra; urethra belongs to the renal axis.
Cryptosporidium infection directly occupies and injures intestinal epithelium; extraintestinal disease is not typical across patients.
Skeletal malformations, intellectual disability and cardiac anomalies define SGS; strabismus and ptosis each occur in 30-79%, supporting ocular involvement.
Hereditary storage myopathy with glycoprotein and glycosaminoglycan accumulation in skeletal muscle; no evidence supplied for common extra-muscular damage.
Arthrogryposis, muscle atrophy and torticollis define the syndrome; cleft palate, conductive hearing loss and ptosis each occur in 30-79%. No demonstrated primary nerve lesion.
Dystroglycanopathy chiefly causes skeletal muscle disease; brain and eye abnormalities vary substantially by subtype and are not established in most across this umbrella.
Familial melanoma predominantly arises in skin; intraocular melanoma is a subtype. Pancreatic and other cancers are separate diseases and occur in a minority.
Severe phenylalanine metabolism defect; untreated neurotoxicity causes intellectual disability in nearly all patients. Prevention by treatment does not negate the natural-course damage.
Localized peripheral chorioretinal degeneration; the affected tissue is ocular even when central vision is preserved.
Activating TSH receptor defect causes pregnancy-triggered thyroid hyperfunction; tachycardia, diarrhea and tremor do not establish damage to additional organs.
SCNN1A-associated bronchiectasis directly damages bronchi; elevated sweat chloride alone does not establish endocrine, metabolic or skin disease.
TYK2-related immunodeficiency defines the disease; respiratory and other infections are separately diagnosed consequences, without established common intrinsic organ damage.
Severe immune dysfunction with profound T/NK-cell deficiency and lymphopenia in 80-99%. Pneumonia and candidiasis are separate infections; diarrhea alone does not establish GI damage.
Acute cocaine poisoning produces central nervous system toxicity and cardiovascular sympathomimetic dysfunction. Infarction, pulmonary injury and rhabdomyolysis are minority complications.
Defined by congenital heart defects, craniosynostosis and developmental impairment; structural tracheal abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting pulmonary involvement.
